# Introduction

Differentiation timing is estimated by projecting bulk RNA-seq samples onto a reference trajectory in principal component analysis (PCA) space. PCA is fitted to the mean expression of temporal genes at each reference timepoint, and the resulting centroids are connected in time order. Each sample's position on the trajectory gives a predicted reference time and a differentiation score from 0 to 1. The projection distance measures fit to the reference.

The analysis uses a cardiomyocyte differentiation time course from GSE122380, with leave-one-cell-line-out validation to assess prediction across cell lines.

# Function inputs

`get_temporal_genes()` requires integer-like raw counts and variance-stabilized (VST) expression with matching gene and sample identifiers. `score_differentiation_timing()` uses normalized expression and the selected temporal genes. In both matrices, rows are genes and columns are samples. Row and column names must be unique, with one metadata row per sample.

The default metadata columns are `sample_id` and `day_numeric`; other names can be specified through `sample_id_col` and `time_col`. The reference must span at least two distinct, finite numeric timepoints. Non-reference samples can have missing timepoints.

The scorer uses all supplied samples as the reference unless `reference_samples` specifies a subset. For comparisons across experimental conditions, gene selection and trajectory fitting are restricted to the reference cohort.

Gene selection requires DESeq2 and edgeR:

```{r install-scoring-dependencies, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
install.packages('BiocManager')
BiocManager::install(c('DESeq2', 'edgeR'))
```

# Reference dataset

[GSE122380](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE122380) contains 192 bulk RNA-seq samples from 13 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines collected over days 1 through 15 of cardiomyocyte differentiation. The metadata, raw counts, and VST expression are included in the [repository](https://github.com/ZohebKhan1/pca-maturation-scoring).

The code runs from the repository root. `load_GSE122380_data()` aligns the count and VST matrices to the metadata sample order:

```{r load-reference-data, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
source('data/load_GSE122380_data.R')
source('functions/get_temporal_genes.R')
source('functions/score_differentiation_timing.R')

reference_data <- load_GSE122380_data()
metadata <- reference_data$metadata
counts <- reference_data$counts
vst <- reference_data$vst
```

```{r sample-summary-table, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
sample_summary <- stats::aggregate(
  sample_id ~ day_numeric,
  data = metadata,
  FUN = length
)
cell_line_summary <- stats::aggregate(
  cell_line ~ day_numeric,
  data = metadata,
  FUN = function(cell_lines) length(unique(cell_lines))
)
data_summary <- merge(sample_summary, cell_line_summary, by = 'day_numeric')
names(data_summary) <- c('day', 'Total samples', 'Unique cell lines')
data_summary <- data_summary[order(data_summary$day), ]

summary_table <- rbind(
  Samples = data_summary[['Total samples']],
  `Cell lines` = data_summary[['Unique cell lines']]
)
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Metric = rownames(summary_table),
  summary_table,
  row.names = NULL,
  check.names = FALSE
)
names(summary_table)[-1] <- paste0('D', data_summary$day)

cat('<div class="table-scroll" role="region" aria-label="Samples and cell lines by differentiation day" tabindex="0">')
knitr::kable(
  summary_table,
  format = 'html',
  table.attr = 'class="sample-summary-table"',
  align = c('l', rep('r', ncol(summary_table) - 1L)),
  caption = 'Samples and represented cell lines by differentiation day.'
)
cat('</div>')
```

PCA of the most variable genes and correlations between day-mean expression profiles show the temporal structure of the reference (Figure 1).

```{r reference-pca-and-correlation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-reference-overview" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_reference_pca_and_day_correlation.png',
  'PCA of the reference samples and a day-level expression correlation heatmap.'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 1.</strong> GSE122380 reference time course and day-level expression correlation. <strong>a.</strong> PCA using the top 10% most variable VST genes, colored by differentiation day. <strong>b.</strong> Pearson correlation between day-mean profiles from the same variable-gene set.</div>

The scoring model uses temporal genes and their mean expression at each timepoint.

# Scoring workflow

## Temporal-gene selection

`get_temporal_genes()` applies three sequential filters within the reference cohort. Raw counts are used for the expression filter and DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test (LRT), and VST expression is used for the range filter. The trajectory model includes genes that pass all three:

1. **Expression filter.** Counts are normalized by the trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) method and expressed as counts per million (CPM). Genes are retained if their highest mean CPM across reference timepoints reaches the expression threshold.
2. **DESeq2 likelihood-ratio test.** The full model includes categorical time and any requested adjustment covariates. The reduced model contains the adjustment covariates without time. Genes with an adjusted LRT p-value below the selected threshold continue to the final filter.
3. **VST-range filter.** Genes are retained if the range of their mean VST expression across reference timepoints reaches the selected threshold.

The LRT tests whether adding categorical time improves the count model. If the full and reduced models have maximized log likelihoods `ell_full` and `ell_reduced`, the likelihood-ratio statistic is

\[
\mathrm{LR} = 2(\ell_\mathrm{full} - \ell_\mathrm{reduced}).
\]

For GSE122380, the full model is `~ cell_line + day_numeric` and the reduced model is `~ cell_line`. Time is converted to a categorical factor, allowing nonlinear expression changes across days. Including `cell_line` in both models accounts for differences among cell lines. With no adjustment covariates, the reduced model is `~ 1`.

```{r temporal-filter-code, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
source('functions/get_temporal_genes.R')

temporal_selection <- get_temporal_genes(
  raw_counts = counts,
  vst_expression = vst,
  metadata = metadata,
  sample_id_col = 'sample_id',
  time_col = 'day_numeric',
  adjustment_covariates = 'cell_line'
)

temporal_genes <- temporal_selection$temporal_genes
```

`reference_group_col` and `reference_group_value` restrict all three filters to a specified group of reference samples.

The default thresholds are a maximum day-mean TMM CPM of at least 10, an adjusted LRT p-value below `1e-7`, and a day-mean VST range of at least 0.6. The number of genes retained at each step is shown in Table 4.1. Thresholds for another study depend on its library sizes, sample size, timepoint coverage, and experimental design.

```{r lrt-summary-table, echo=FALSE}
lrt_display <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    'Genes in the aligned count/VST input',
    'Genes with maximum day-mean TMM CPM >= 10',
    'Genes passing LRT adjusted p-value < 1e-7',
    'Genes passing all filters and used for scoring'
  ),
  Value = c(
    format(lrt_summary$input_genes, big.mark = ','),
    format(lrt_summary$genes_passing_day_mean_tmm_cpm, big.mark = ','),
    format(lrt_summary$genes_passing_lrt_padj, big.mark = ','),
    format(lrt_summary$genes_passing_all_filters, big.mark = ',')
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  lrt_display,
  format = 'html',
  table.attr = 'class="sample-summary-table"',
  align = c('l', 'r'),
  caption = 'Sequential temporal-gene filtering.'
)
```

cat('<div id="fig-temporal-clusters" class="figure-anchor"></div>')

## Reference PCA

The reference PCA is fitted to mean temporal-gene expression at each timepoint. Each timepoint contributes one expression profile to the fit, regardless of its sample count.

Let \(\mathbf{x}_i\) be the normalized expression vector for sample \(i\), restricted to the selected temporal genes. For a reference timepoint \(t\), let \(\bar{\mathbf{x}}_t\) be the mean vector across its reference samples:

\[
\bar{\mathbf{x}}_t = \frac{1}{n_t}\sum_{i:\,t_i=t} \mathbf{x}_i.
\tag{1}
\]

PCA is centered without variance scaling. The smallest number of principal components (PCs) explaining at least 99% of the variance between timepoint means is retained. With \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) denoting the mean of those profiles and \(W\) the retained loading vectors, the PCA coordinates for sample \(i\) are

\[
\mathbf{z}_i = (\mathbf{x}_i - \boldsymbol{\mu})W.
\tag{2}
\]

Reference and experimental samples are projected using the same centering and loadings. Seven PCs meet the 99% variance target in GSE122380; the retained number depends on the reference cohort and temporal-gene set.

```{r pca-day, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-pca-day" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_pca_day.png',
  'PCA and PC1 versus day for all temporal genes and early and late cluster subsets.'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 4.</strong> Individual samples projected into centered, unscaled PCA spaces fitted to reference timepoint means. The full temporal-gene set defines the scoring model. The C1+C2 and C3+C4 subsets show how early and late expression patterns contribute to the time-course structure.</div>

Figure 5 shows genes with the largest positive and negative PC1 and PC2 loadings, with GO enrichment for the strongest PC1 loadings.

```{r pc1-validation, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-pc1-validation" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_pc1_validation.png',
  'Top PCA loading genes and GO enrichment for positive and negative PC1 loadings.'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 5.</strong> PCA loading genes and GO enrichment. <strong>a-b.</strong> The ten largest positive and negative PC1 and PC2 loading genes. Ambiguous Ensembl-to-symbol mappings retain the Ensembl ID. <strong>c-d.</strong> GO enrichment among the 500 strongest negative and positive PC1 loadings.</div>

PC1 is oriented toward increasing differentiation day in the figures. This choice of axis sign preserves distances and timing scores.

## Trajectory fitting and sample projection

The reference timepoint means define centroids in the retained PCA space. Connecting adjacent centroids in time order produces a polyline trajectory that can bend across multiple PCs.

For one segment, let \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\) be its start and end centroids, and let \(\mathbf{z}\) be a sample's PCA coordinate. The segment direction is \(\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}\). The closest point on the finite segment is

\[
\alpha = \operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}
\left(
\frac{\langle \mathbf{z}-\mathbf{a},\mathbf{v}\rangle}
     {\langle \mathbf{v},\mathbf{v}\rangle}
\right),
\qquad
\mathbf{q}=\mathbf{a}+\alpha\mathbf{v}.
\tag{3}
\]

The projection is clipped to each finite segment by constraining \(\alpha\) between 0 and 1. The segment minimizing \(\lVert\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{q}\rVert^2\) determines the sample's assignment, and its endpoint times are used to interpolate predicted time:

\[
\widehat{t}=t_a+\alpha(t_b-t_a),
\qquad
s=\frac{\widehat{t}-t_{\min}}{t_{\max}-t_{\min}}.
\tag{4}
\]

Here, \(t_a\) and \(t_b\) are the segment endpoint times, \(\widehat{t}\) is predicted time, and \(s\) is the differentiation score. Scores are bounded between 0 and 1, corresponding to the earliest and latest reference times.

Zero-length segments are omitted. If the trajectory folds back near itself, nearby segments can yield ambiguous time assignments even when projection distances are small.

```{r timing-score-code, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
source('functions/score_differentiation_timing.R')

timing_fit <- score_differentiation_timing(
  expression_matrix = vst,
  metadata = metadata,
  temporal_genes = temporal_genes,
  sample_id_col = 'sample_id',
  time_col = 'day_numeric'
)

timing_fit$scores[, c(
  'sample_id',
  'observed_time',
  'predicted_time',
  'differentiation_score',
  'squared_distance'
)]
```

Figure 6 displays the first two PCs of the fitted trajectory. Projection distances are calculated across all retained PCs.

```{r timing-polyline, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-timing-polyline" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_timing_polyline.png',
  'Samples and the ordered day-centroid polyline in the first two principal components.',
  '86%'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 6.</strong> Differentiation trajectory in reference PCA space. Black points are day centroids; arrows connect them in day order. The day 1 and day 15 centroids anchor scores 0 and 1.</div>

Time is interpolated separately within each segment, allowing distances per unit time to vary across intervals. Figure 7 shows the reference samples projected back onto the fitted trajectory.

```{r score-by-day, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-score-by-day" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_score_by_day.png',
  'Differentiation timing scores across observed differentiation days.'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 7.</strong> Reference-sample differentiation timing scores by observed day. Dashed lines mark the bounded reference endpoints at 0 and 1.</div>

These scores describe fit within the reference cohort. Prediction in held-out samples is assessed by leave-one-cell-line-out validation.

# Leave-one-cell-line-out validation

Each cell line is held out in turn. Temporal-gene selection, including the DESeq2 LRT, and PCA trajectory fitting are repeated using the remaining cell lines. The held-out samples are then projected onto that fold's reference trajectory.

All folds share the supplied VST matrix because the upstream transformation procedure is unavailable in the repository. Validation therefore assesses transfer across cell lines within this processed cohort, conditional on the shared transformation. Transfer to an independently processed study requires separate validation.

Within each fold, genes with positive and negative Spearman correlations with time are labeled maturation and progenitor genes, respectively. Reported accuracy uses the complete temporal-gene set selected in that fold.

```{r loo-code, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
source('functions/get_temporal_genes.R')
source('functions/score_differentiation_timing.R')
source('functions/run_loo_maturation.R')

loo_validation <- run_loo_maturation(
  counts = counts,
  vst = vst,
  metadata = metadata
)

loo_validation$summary
```

The summary includes held-out predictions for all 13 cell lines. Figure 8 displays 12 cell lines in a 3 by 4 layout; predictions for cell line `19190` are included in the summary and the remaining validation figures.

```{r loo-summary-table, echo=FALSE}
loo_display_summary <- loo_accuracy_summary
names(loo_display_summary) <- c('Metric', 'Value')
knitr::kable(
  loo_display_summary,
  format = 'html',
  table.attr = 'class="sample-summary-table"',
  align = c('l', 'r'),
  caption = 'Leave-one-cell-line-out validation summary.'
)
```

Held-out predictions have a Pearson correlation of 0.979 with observed days, a median absolute error of 0.30 days, and 82.3% of predictions within one day. These estimates apply to GSE122380 under the processing and validation scheme described above.

```{r loo-cell-line-predictions, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-loo-cell-line-predictions" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_loo_cell_line_predictions.png',
  'Predicted versus observed day trajectories for twelve displayed held-out cell lines.'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 8.</strong> Held-out predictions for 12 cell lines. Each panel reports Pearson \(r\) and squared Pearson correlation, \(r^2\), to summarize linear association between observed and predicted days.</div>

Pearson \(r\) and \(r^2\) summarize association, while absolute prediction error measures accuracy on the day scale. Figures 9 and 10 show the pooled predictions and errors by day.

```{r loo-summary-figure, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-loo-summary" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_loo_summary.png',
  'Predicted versus observed differentiation day for every held-out sample.'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 9.</strong> Predicted versus observed differentiation day for all held-out samples. The dashed line is identity; the solid line is an ordinary least-squares summary.</div>

For held-out sample \(i\), absolute prediction error is

\[
e_i = |\widehat{t}_i - t_i|.
\tag{5}
\]

Figure 10 shows mean absolute error by differentiation day, with error bars representing one standard deviation across held-out samples.

```{r loo-timepoint-accuracy, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('<div id="fig-loo-timepoint-accuracy" class="figure-anchor"></div>')
tutorial_figure(
  'GSE122380_loo_timepoint_accuracy.png',
  'Mean absolute held-out prediction error by observed differentiation day, with standard-deviation error bars.',
  '82%'
)
```

<div class="tutorial-figure-caption"><strong>Figure 10.</strong> Absolute held-out prediction error by day.</div>

# Interpreting results

## Scores and projection distances

`timing_fit$scores` contains the sample-level estimates:

- `predicted_time` gives the sample's position on the original reference-time scale.
- `differentiation_score` rescales that position so the earliest and latest reference times are 0 and 1.
- `squared_distance` measures how close the sample is to its nearest trajectory segment in the retained PCA space.

Scores are specific to the reference lineage, differentiation protocol, and sampled time range. Comparisons across conditions require a shared reference model.

A large projection distance relative to reference samples indicates poor fit to the trajectory and limits the interpretation of predicted time. Differences in cell composition, treatment response, or batch can produce these deviations.

## Reference selection for another study

For comparisons across conditions, temporal-gene selection and trajectory fitting use an independent reference group. The following example identifies that group through a metadata column named `group`, with reference samples labeled `reference`. Here, `counts`, `vst`, and `metadata` contain aligned reference and experimental samples from the new study, with the same `sample_id` and `day_numeric` columns used above:

```{r score-study-samples, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
temporal_selection <- get_temporal_genes(
  raw_counts = counts,
  vst_expression = vst,
  metadata = metadata,
  reference_group_col = 'group',
  reference_group_value = 'reference'
)

timing_fit <- score_differentiation_timing(
  expression_matrix = vst,
  metadata = metadata,
  temporal_genes = temporal_selection$temporal_genes,
  reference_samples = temporal_selection$reference_samples
)
```

Experimental samples can have missing timepoints. Adjustment covariates can be included in gene selection when supported by the reference design.

The reference should span the relevant differentiation stages and use gene identifiers and normalization compatible with the experimental samples. Differences in protocol, cell composition, or batch can alter scores and projection distances. Application to a substantially different dataset requires validation in that setting.

3. Strober BJ, Elorbany R, Rhodes K, et al. Dynamic genetic regulation of gene expression during cellular differentiation. *Science*. 2019;364(6447):1287–1290. [doi:10.1126/science.aaw0040](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaw0040)
